title: "Frequently observed around nuclear platforms": Alien life would have harmed us already if intended, says former admiral Timothy Gallaudet
excerpt: Alien life, the possibility of its existence, and how it might affect us have been topics of interest for decades. While innumerable conspiracy theories have been made over the years, we are yet to receive concrete proof of the existence of extraterrestrial life.
content:

Updated Wed, October 28, 2026 at 9:26 PM UTC

Alien life, the possibility of its existence, and how it might affect us have been topics of interest for decades. While innumerable conspiracy theories have been made over the years, we are yet to receive concrete proof of the existence of extraterrestrial life. Alien life is also being researched heavily right now, with a UAP science advisory council in place that recommends the release of more data on extraterrestrial life.

Former Navy Rear Admiral Timothy Gallaudet is a part of the council and knows more than others regarding Alien life and what it could potentially mean for us. Gallaudet has recently revealed that he thinks Alien life could have harmed us already if they wanted to.

Alien life might have motivations we cannot yet anticipate

On Hang Out with Sean Hannity, Timothy Gallaudet spoke with Hannity about extraterrestrial life, if and what the military knows about it, and unidentified objects in American airspace. Gallaudet said that he was part of a UAP Science Advisory Council convened by the administration that reported to the Office of the Director of National Intelligence.

He explained that the council's objective was to recommend the release of more data so that researchers could study the phenomenon and better understand it. Hannity then noted that Gallaudet had previously stated that he believed that these entities were interacting with humans. Moreover, Hannity added that he had read extensively about alleged abductions and claims that the extraterrestrial beings wanted to make contact with humans.

Hannity suggested that the extraterrestrial beings were in complete control, and Gallaudet agreed. Gallaudet said that he believes that every alleged incident has happened entirely on their terms. He added that the difficult part about the situation was that it was not really repeatable. As in, the authorities could not scientifically create an experiment to demonstrate what the extraterrestrial beings were potentially doing.

Gallaudet stated that extraterrestrial beings have not yet fully revealed themselves or explained their agenda, which is why their intentions remain unclear. Following up on that, Hannity asked if it would be fair to assume that if Alien life wanted to harm or kill us, they would have done so already.

Gallaudet responded by saying that he thought that was a possibility because according to him, some nuclear sites have been disarmed. Referring to unidentified objects being seen, he said:

"Frequently observed around nuclear platforms."

Gallaudet said these unidentified objects were observed around aircraft carriers and ballistic missile submarines. He said he knows firsthand witnesses who had approached him and described their experiences of interacting with these unidentified objects while serving aboard such submarines.

Gallaudet added that, thankfully, these unidentified objects or extraterrestrial beings have not taken out an aircraft carrier or a ballistic missile submarine, which could harm us. However, he did note that the extraterrestrial beings' frequent presence around these facilities and platforms suggested that they were interested in them.

He concluded that he does believe that if Alien life wanted to kill us, they would have done so already. But since they haven't harmed us yet, we can't guess what their true intentions are.

Gallaudet's words do carry weight, but they do not confirm or deny the existence of extraterrestrial life. The US government has been making efforts towards releasing more information about the alleged existence of Alien life, and we will hopefully know more on the topic soon.
